name: CR-Diff-09-misc-6.b
questiontext:
Find the following derivative:
\[ \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}({{CT:1}}). \]
Hint: write \(sec(v)\) as \(1/{{CT:2}}\)

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Since \({{CT:3}}=\frac{1}{{CT:2}}\), \({{CT:1}}=\frac{1}{{CT:2}}^{{CT:4}}\)

So, using the chain rule <hint>calc_chain_rule</hint> and the quotient rule <hint>calc_quotient_rule</hint>,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}({{CT:1}}) &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[\left(\frac{1}{{CT:2}}\right)^{{CT:4}}\right] \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:4}}\left[\frac{1}{{CT:2}}\right]^{({{CT:4}}-1)}\cdot \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[\frac{1}{{CT:2}}\right] \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{{CT:4}}{{{CT:2}}^{{CT:5}}}\cdot \frac{\frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[1]\cdot {{CT:2}}-1\cdot \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[{{CT:2}}]}{{{CT:2}}^2} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:6}}\cdot \frac{0-{{CT:7}}}{{CT:8}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:9}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:10}}
 \end{array}\]

You have to use the chain rule <hint>calc_chain_rule</hint> to differentiate {{CT:11}} with respect to {{CT:12}}.
